No, the ocean is not acidic, not subject to "acidification" (whatever that is) nor will it ever be. It is alkaline.

Acidification is the process of something becoming more acidic, or less basic, on the pH scale.

It's related to increases in CO2 emissions. One of the things keeping CO2 levels from getting really insane for now is the ocean. It absorbs a good chunk of CO2 but that results in a chemical reaction. The CO2 interacts with the ocean water and forms carbonic acid - H2CO3. The carbonic acid reacts with water to give bicarbonate and hydronium ions (CO3 -2 and H30 +1 respectively) ions. The hydronium results in an increase in hydrogen ions and thus the acidification.

It's not going turn the ocean into an acid any time soon, but it is real and a very serious concern.
